reviews.title: Syncing with other devices doesn't work well
reviews.text: Scrivener is a good word processor for writing. This app claims to sync with projects on other devices so that you can write anywhere. That may technically be true, deep in some nested menu somewhere it may be possible to sync. I fussed with it for 2 days and had no luck.

reviews.title: No update for far too long again! 3 yrs!
reviews.text: I have been using Scrivener for many years, and throughout those years there have been minimal updates. It’s been frustrating. And now there is an issue where I try to search for a word in my project, or use find and replace, and the box shows for a millisecond and disappears again. So I currently can’t use the feature which is quite a big problem. And now I know that it’s going to be like that for a long time due to the history of non-existent updates! Also, still no sign of them using a different cloud storage. Probably the only app that doesn’t use apple cloud or google drive as a back up option. Limited to Dropbox, which I haven’t used for years! How is this still a thing in 2026? I really need to find an alternative to this, which is a real shame because if the company actually put some care into this, it’s a great app, and could be even better. Seems they don’t care at all. 3 years since the last update (for ios17!) is unacceptable from an app that wasn’t cheap.

reviews.title: Sucks at syncing!!
reviews.text: This app (Mac, iPhone, iPad) has terrible syncing problems with Dropbox. I’m constantly getting error messages about syncing problems, despite me closing the app at the end of use and saving, and never having the document open on two devices at the same time. About once a month I lose edits because they fail to sync what I edited or wrote. I don’t understand why we’re in 2026 and this app sucks so much at syncing. Ditch Dropbox, and use the Apple method of syncing like every other modern app. I never have problems like this on Notes.

reviews.title: Cross-Platform data loss
reviews.text: This app has not been updated for two years and the small problems with modern iPad OS are starting to add up. In addition, the Dropbox sync options between iPad and Desktop use outdated APIs that generate persistent conflicts — in some cases deleting work. The official answer on the forums has been “You have a backup, right?” Which is not acceptable for an application suite that advertises being able to switch between Desktop and iPad. At this point, Scrivener for iPad has be come almost unusable and has resulted in at least one loss of a week’s worth of work. I would consider this application currently UNSUPPORTED until they get a new update out. If you are only working on iPad, there are still issues with missing features (keywords) and limited compile options (the very powerful compilation features of the desktop app are the only reason I have stuck with Scrivener for so long).

reviews.title: Limited Potential
reviews.text:
The App has been amazing. Being able to use Scrivener on the go is incredible. Picking up where I left off on multiple devices makes writing convenient beyond measure. Everything syncs quickly, effortlessly and easily. However, there are a few inconsistencies to address. First, some fonts are not shared between mobile and desktop so when syncing, text revert to a shared fonts. 
Second, the features on iPhone/iPad are clunky and outdated. Such as changing colors, font, line spacing and layout. 
Third, The “mobile” versions are essentially watered down version of the desktop. You lose a lot of features such as viewing your corkboard, viewing multiple folders, and other key features Scrivener has to offer. 
Fourth, this has been an ongoing issue for months. I cannot even use the built in app shortcuts! It’s so frustrating I can’t use highlighting, insert, font changes, etc. I’ve reached out multiple times and avenues and been seen and ignored. 
I hope the developers are able to make the desktop and mobile versions more alike in sense of having similar functionality, we understand they may not be exactly the same but any update for desktop features would make this rating a Five Star easily. Fix the app issues. 
Thank you.

reviews.title: Rarely Updated
reviews.text:
Update: here we are years later and there is still no updates. So as the OS improves this become more and more buggy. Sync begins to suck and cause issues no matter how certain you are at making sure Dropbox is updated first. They are so frustrating that they care so little about the customers to keep a program without updating it. It should be updated at least once a year at a minimum. 



I wrote this years ago and the issue of losing content or errors (even when fully synced) still exists. Good software companies should update their software at least a few times a year to both squash bugs and add new features. It’s ridiculous this hasn’t been updated in years. 


The biggest issue is that the software is rarely updated, which means bugs linger indefinitely. I’ve stopped writing in it daily because sync problems between the desktop and cloud inevitably cause errors. I’ve lost entire chapters. Now, I only use it to store the most recent version of my work, since relying on it for everyday writing leads to constant conflicts I can’t afford to deal with.

Some sycophants claim the software doesn’t need frequent updates, but that’s simply not true. All software has bugs, and they need to be fixed regularly. This program hasn’t been updated in over a year, and in the past, it’s gone several years without a single update. For one of the most popular writing tools outside of traditional word processors, the lack of care from the developers is unacceptable.

reviews.title: Is It Abandoned? YES, ABANDONED! BOOOOO!
reviews.text: An App rarely out of the Top Ten in the Productivity section of the App Store is earning the developers large money. Therefore, why is none of it being reinvested in keeping the app updated, upgraded and generally looked after? Is this now a metaphorical cash-cow until the herd come home? Sad state of affairs, and the long promised iOS version of the sister app ‘Scapple’ has still not materialised either! Is there actually anyone left at this company, or is this now a run-down asset? Seriously, I’d like to know; if I’m to trust an app with 1000’s of hours of labour, I want to know it’s going to receive some care!

reviews.title: I shouldn’t have to buy it twice
reviews.text:
First things first: if you ONLY plan to write on your iPad, then this is 100% the right software for you. 

I, however, discovered this software while I was away from home, without my desktop. I paid for it and found it to be an excellent writing tool. I even synced with my Dropbox in advance so I could continue seamlessly when I finally returned home to my laptop. 

When that day finally came, I discovered that I would have to pay an additional $60 to install it on my computer. 

I am completely blown away by this. I can imagine the opposing argument: macOS and iPadOS versions are independent products, different code base, etc. 

That said, the modern digital world has created the expectation that users of digital software be able move between devices seamlessly. 

When a customer purchases software, they’re primarily buying access to the product’s functionality and ecosystem, not a specific compilation of code for a particular device. In 2026, consumers have become accustomed to software licenses following their account across phones, tablets, laptops, and the web, especially within the same platform family like Apple’s ecosystem. Charging $25 for the iPad version and then requiring an additional $60 for the Mac version is not justifiable when I’m not really paying for new software; I’m just paying a second admission fee to use the same writing tool on another screen. reviews.title: Syncing Issues Make the iOS App Hard to Trust
reviews.text:
I really wanted to like this app, but the syncing issues make it unreliable for real work.

The entire purpose of having Scrivener on iPad is to continue writing when you’re away from your Mac. Unfortunately, that simply doesn’t work consistently. Projects that open perfectly fine on the Mac show up as “invalid project” on iPad, even when the binder file exists and Dropbox reports everything fully synced.

I followed every troubleshooting step provided by support: clearing the sync cache, reinstalling the app, verifying the binder file, closing projects before syncing, testing new projects, and confirming that all files were available offline. The problem still persists across multiple projects and multiple iPads.

The most concerning part is that the iOS app has not been meaningfully updated in years. Meanwhile, Dropbox, macOS, and iPadOS continue to evolve. When a core feature like syncing becomes unreliable, the app stops being practical for writers who need to move between devices.

Scrivener itself is powerful software on Mac. But if you are buying the iOS version expecting a seamless writing workflow between your Mac and iPad, you should know that syncing problems are still very real.

Until the iOS version receives active development and reliable syncing, it’s difficult to recommend.

reviews.title: Abandonware
reviews.text: I hate to lower the star average on this otherwise wonderful author-oriented text editing iPad app, however since iPadOS 26 debuted last fall, the app has suffered from issues with Find (⌘F). I noted them first in beta, and I posted to the forums. Now, with 26.2 out for weeks (I am using the release version of iPadOS, now), still no bug fix update issued. Using Find often but intermittently causes the find window to show then hide itself. If it does show, using it a few times can lock up the app until it quits and restarts. It appears to be related to the Windowed Apps feature, but it happens even with the feature turned off. Lit & Latte has updated the Mac version repeatedly, but why not the iOS/iPadOS version? It feels like they've abandoned it. Think about it, what kind of revision can you do without search and search and replace working? I am using the M5 iPad Pro 13", but it failed on my earlier iPad, too. I do not recommend buying the app for sole iPad use, nor if you need to use it for syncing between Apple platforms. The Mac version has no issues. I will revise this review once the issue is fixed.

reviews.title: Mis-understood
reviews.text:
This is partly on me, but I was also misled. I’ve already written my first book, about 75,000 words, and I’ve struggled to get the format to paginate. Pages on iOS doesn’t do this on the iPad, which led me to this app. It’s advertised as the best iPad app for writing a book, “written for writers by writers,” so I assumed they knew what they were doing. I paid full price, being fully aware that many reviews mentioned a steep learning curve. That didn’t bother me, I’m very familiar with Apple devices.

After two hours of YouTube Scrivener tutorials, most spending twenty minutes talking about themselves and another fifteen showing how to open the app and create a blank file(very painful to watch) I finally got impatient. I asked AI (which I probably should’ve done from the start) how pagination works in Scrivener, only to learn that Scrivener doesn’t do it at all. It’s really just a drafting tool, not something that helps with final formatting when you’re preparing to publish. Its strengths are in organization, not page layout.

I’m not thrilled about leaving only two stars because part of this was my own misunderstanding. But that’s exactly why I’m writing this review, to spare a few others the same headache. The app is professionally built, and if you need help organizing all the thoughts and pieces that go into writing a book, it might serve you well. For me, though, it’s just another app I don’t need on my iPad and will forget the pain it caused me. When all is said and done
